findings.description: The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management port of the instance to the entire internet.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no additional restriction, which may be intentional for a web server but combined with SSH exposure and no compensating controls broadens the attack surface unnecessarily.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (all protocols, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext within the EC2 user_data script, which is readable by anyone with DescribeInstanceAttribute permissions and is also stored in Terraform state, exposing long-lived static credentials.
The instance does not configure metadata_options to require IMDSv2 (http_tokens = required), leaving the legacy instance metadata service enabled and vulnerable to SSRF-based credential theft.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of workloads to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of workloads to the internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a kms_key_id, so data at rest on this volume is unencrypted by default.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving stored log data unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access controls / public access block
findings.description: The bucket has no public access block, bucket policy, or ACL restrictions defined, and force_destroy = true allows destruction of log data; absence of explicit access controls risks the bucket being left with permissive defaults.

The default route sends all outbound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) through the internet gateway for a route table associated with subnets hosting the instance, reinforcing the public exposure of resources in these subnets.
